text: Design (no code) how Athena classifies, organizes and applies its decisions, from the BRIEF.md addendum '2026-10-13: Decision sets, and knowing when a decision is not working'. Write docs/design/decision-sets.md. Today decisions live apart and only defaults are applied: BRIEF.md addenda, defaults.toml (12), docs/decisions.md (D01-D90, a flat log whose supersessions live only in prose), and corrections inside job records. Give every decision typed fields (kind: requirement, expectation, design or process; scope: classes of work, paths and phase such as reading, producing, verifying, landing; status: active, proposed or superseded by a named decision; source; enforcement: code check, brief, or prose only). Group decisions into sets by scope, and apply a set's active decisions to a role's brief when a job matches its scope, the way defaults are applied now; defaults become one kind of decision. Also, so Athena cannot be confidently wrong: each decision states its assumptions and the observable signals that would show it is failing; Athena watches those signals in its records (rejections, interventions, corrections, check failures, host errors), and a firing signal puts the decision under review instead of leaving it applied. Example: D87 chose merge commits without stating that it assumed the repository allows them, and GitHub refused with HTTP 405 within the hour. Fit this with docs/design/defaults-loop.md, its introspection step and Jev (/v1/evaluate) for set membership and signal matching. Cover how the existing decisions are migrated, and keep within the reader's token budget.
